summary: A dropdown over a native <select>, with the same label and error wiring as Input.
useWhen: the user picks exactly one value from a known, modest list
the native platform picker is acceptable — and on mobile it usually is the best option

useInstead.when: the list is long enough to need search or type-ahead beyond the native behaviour
useInstead.use: a combobox — not yet in this system

useInstead.when: the rows need icons, avatars or two lines of text
useInstead.why: Select wraps a native <select>, whose options can only be text

useInstead.when: there are two or three mutually exclusive choices worth showing at once
the user may pick more than one

guarantees: keyboard handling, type-ahead and the mobile platform picker come from the native <select> rather than being reimplemented
label, helper and error wiring match Input
requires: `label`, or `aria-label` when no visible label is rendered

antiPatterns.dont: passing rich React nodes as option content
antiPatterns.why: this renders a native <select>; options are text only

antiPatterns.dont: using a Select with two options for an on/off setting
antiPatterns.why: a two-item dropdown costs two interactions to do what one control does in one
